title: Yashin Trophy: Full List of Winners, Most Wins of All Time
subtitle: SI
paragraphs: By Amanda LangellSep 8, 2026Unai Simón won the first Yashin Trophy of his career in 2026.  / Franck Fife/AFP/Getty ImagesGoalkeepers across the men’s and women’s game all hope to one day take home the Yashin Trophy, awarded annually to the top shot-stoppers in the sport.

Created in 2019, the award was named after Lev Yashin, the only goalkeeper to ever take home the Ballon d’Or. Each year since, the best male goalkeeper in the world was honored with the prize, only pausing in 2020 due to the Covid-19 pandemic.
Six years later, the Women’s Yashin Trophy was established to also crown the best female shot-stoppers in the game.
Only five individuals had ever won the illustrious prizes, but two new elite shot-stoppers took home the pair of awards at the 2026 Ballon d’Or ceremony.
Here’s a breakdown of the award’s history.

Gianluigi Donnarumma is one of the two goalkeepers that have won the Yashin Trophy multiple times.  / Franck Fife/AFP/Getty ImagesGianluigi Donnarumma and Emiliano Martínez lead the way with two Men’s Yashin Trophy awards each. The former took home the award for the first time in 2021 after Italy’s European Championship triumph before he added a second to his trophy cabinet four years later for his contributions in goal for Paris Saint-Germain’s historic quadruple in 2024–25.

Martínez, meanwhile, is the only player to win the award in back-to-back years. The shot-stopper claimed the prize in 2023 and 2024 largely for his efforts in goal for Argentina. La Albiceleste won the 2022 World Cup and then the 2024 Copa América.

In 2026, Unai Simón became the fifth goalkeeper in history to win the Men’s Yashin Trophy. Although he conceded over 50 goals last season with Athletic Club, Simón was spectacular at the 2026 World Cup, conceding just once in eight games to help Spain lift the most prestigious trophy in the sport.
Thibaut Courtois and Alisson are the only other goalkeepers ever to take home the prize.
Barcelona Femení goalkeeper Cata Coll took home the 2026 Women’s Yashin trophy.  / Jeff Spicer/UEFA/Getty ImagesYear

Hannah Hampton won the inaugural Women’s Yashin Trophy. / Franck Fife/AFP/Getty ImagesIn 2026, Barcelona Femení goalkeeper Cata Coll became the second winner of the Women’s Yashin Trophy. Coll conceded just six goals in 17 league games as Barcelona continued their dominance over Spanish soccer with a historic quadruple. She also kept a clean sheet in Barcelona’s 4–0 win against OL Lyonnes in the 2025–26 Champions League final.

Hannah Hampton made history in 2025 when she became the first recipient of the Women’s Yashin Trophy. The goalkeeper took home the prize after a sensational 2024–25 campaign in which she won a domestic treble for Chelsea and was between the sticks as England conquered the 2025 European Championship.
